Pro Forma Large Load Security Agreement

44.16.10 Appendix 10 to Attachment LL – Pro Forma Security Agreement 
 
PRO FORMA LARGE LOAD SECURITY AGREEMENT 
BETWEEN 
[NEW YORK TRANSMISSION OWNER] 
(Transmission Owner) 
AND 
[CUSTOMER NAME] 
(Customer)

TABLE OF CONTENTS 
Recitals 
Article I: Definitions 
Article II: Security 
Article III: Term 
Article IV: Notices 
Article V: Miscellaneous 
• Schedule 1: Project Security Amount and Posting Schedule 
• Attachment A: Form of Irrevocable Standby Letter of Credit 
• Attachment B: Related Agreement

PRO FORMA 
LARGE LOAD SECURITY AGREEMENT 
This LARGE LOAD SECURITY AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”) is made and entered into 
as of the [___] day of [_______], 20[__] (the “Effective Date”) by and between: 
• [NEW YORK TRANSMISSION OWNER] (“Transmission Owner” or “Connecting 
Transmission Owner” or “Affected Transmission Owner”), a [corporation] organized and 
existing under the laws of the State of New York, having an office and place of business at 
[_________]; and  
• [CUSTOMER NAME] (“Customer”), a [corporation/ limited liability company] 
organized under the laws of the State of [_____], having an office and place of business at 
[______], and owning a Large Load Facility with an expected peak demand at the Point of 
Interconnection.  
Transmission Owner and Customer are collectively referred to as the “Parties,” and each 
individually as a “Party.” 
RECITALS 
WHEREAS, Customer has submitted a Large Load Integration Request to interconnect or serve 
a Large Load Facility with an aggregate demand equal to or exceeding fifty megawatts (50 MW) 
at a transmission-system interconnection point with the Transmission Owner’s service territory or 
affecting the Affected Transmission Owner’s transmission facilities in New York State;  
WHEREAS, New York Independent System Operator, Inc. (“NYISO”) and/or Transmission 
Owner have performed [system reliability impact studies, facility studies, and/or engineering 
assessments] pursuant to the NYISO Open Access Transmission Tariff (“OATT”), identifying that 
the interconnection and commercial operation of Customer’s Large Load Facility will necessitate 
the construction and placement into service of certain Network Upgrades and/or TO Attachment 
Facilities on the Transmission Owner’s transmission system to maintain electric system reliability 
and system adequacy; and  
WHEREAS, Customer has received the initial cost allocation estimate for Network Upgrades 
and/or TO Attachment Facilities identified by System Impact Studies and any applicable Facilities 
Studies under Attachment LL of the NYISO OATT or successor tariff provisions needed to 
interconnect Customer’s Large Load Facility; 
WHEREAS, Customer is required to post security to Transmission Owner in the initial amount 
of [      ] Dollars ($[     ]), (the “Initial Project Security Amount”), consistent with Attachment 
LL of the NYISO OATT;  
WHEREAS, the Initial Project Security Amount is subject to adjustment in accordance with the 
Interconnection Cost Allocation Process as set forth in Section [__] of Attachment LL of the 
NYISO OATT (the “Project Security Amount”);  
WHEREAS, the Project Security Amount may thereafter be adjusted pursuant to the Large Load 
Cost Recovery Agreement (“CRA”), into which Customer has entered or will enter and pursuant

to which it will agree to pay for all of Transmission Owner’s costs associated with the development 
of Network Upgrades and/or TO Attachment Facilities;  
WHEREAS, Customer’s obligations to post Security under this Agreement shall be set forth in 
Schedule 1;  
WHEREAS, Customer may also enter into a Large Load Interconnection Agreement or other 
applicable agreement(s) governing, among other things, the construction of the Network Upgrades 
and/or TO Attachment Facilities; and  
WHEREAS, the Parties desire to set forth in this Agreement the terms governing the posting, 
maintenance, adjustment, application and release of such Security. 
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the premises and for other good and valuable 
consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, and with the intent 
to be legally bound, the Parties agree as follows: 
ARTICLE I: DEFINITIONS 
1.0 
Defined Terms. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Agreement have the 
meanings given in the NYISO OATT, NYISO Market Services Tariff, or, if not defined 
therein, in the CRA or applicable Large Load Interconnection Agreement, if those 
agreements are in effect.  
1.1  
“Abandon” means Customer’s (i) failure to issue a notice to proceed for Transmission 
Owner to commence construction of the Project Facilities within [six (6)] months after the 
applicable construction commencement milestone set forth in Exhibit D of the Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement, or (ii) suspension of, or causing the suspension of, 
construction of the Project Facilities for a period of [three (3)] years, which, in either case, 
is not due to an event of Force Majeure; provided that if Force Majeure causes such failure 
or suspension, Customer shall nevertheless be deemed to have abandoned construction if 
it fails to commence or resume construction within [six (6)] months after the end of the 
Force Majeure event (unless Customer has elected to continue such suspension for a total 
suspension period not exceeding [three (3)] years in accordance with the Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement or CRA). 
1.2  
“Affiliate” means, with respect to a person or entity, any other person or entity directly or 
indirectly controlling, controlled by, or under common control with such person or entity. 
“Control” means the possession, directly or indirectly, of the power to direct the 
management or policies of a person or entity; a voting interest of ten percent (10%) or more 
creates a rebuttable presumption of control. 
1.3  
“Business Day” means any day except Saturday, Sunday, a U.S. federal legal holiday, or 
a day on which banking institutions in the State of New York are authorized or required by 
law or other governmental action to close. 
1.4 
“Cash” means readily available United States dollars delivered by wire transfer in 
accordance with Transmission Owner’s written instructions.  Transmission Owner’s 
written instructions can be delivered via email or other means of electronic communication.  
1.5  
“CRA” means the Large Load Cost Recovery Agreement.

1.6  
“Credit Rating” means, with respect to an entity on any date of determination, the rating 
assigned to that entity’s unsecured, senior long-term debt (not supported by third-party 
credit enhancement) or its corporate credit rating, whichever is lower, by S&P or Moody’s. 
If the entity is rated by both S&P and Moody’s, the lower rating controls; if it is rated by 
only one, that rating controls. For a financial institution that is the issuer of a letter of credit 
hereunder, the applicable rating is its long-term deposit rating or senior unsecured, 
unsubordinated long-term debt rating, as applicable. 
1.7  
“Creditworthy Rating” means a Credit Rating of at least the threshold selected in 
Schedule 1: [as acceptable to the Transmission Owner]. 
1.8  
“Cure Period” means the applicable notice and cure period under the relevant Related 
Agreement and, with respect to this Agreement, five (5) Business Days after Transmission 
Owner’s written notice. 
1.9  
“Event of Default” means an Event of Default under the CRA or a Default under the Large 
Load Interconnection Agreement. 
1.10  “FERC” means the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. 
1.11 
“Force Majeure” means any event or circumstance beyond a Party’s reasonable control 
that prevents the Party from performing an obligation, is not the result of the negligence or 
intentional wrongdoing of such Party, and could not have been prevented or mitigated by 
the exercise of Good Utility Practice (in the case of the Transmission Owner) or due 
diligence (in the case of Customer), including acts of God, fire, flood, storm, lightning, 
explosion, breakage of or accident to machinery, epidemic or pandemic, cyber-attack 
(except to the extent caused by or resulting from Customer’s failure to comply with its 
obligations under this Agreement), sabotage, terrorism, war, civil disturbance, strikes and 
labor disturbances, acts or orders of any Governmental Authority, and curtailment or 
interruption directed by NYISO for reliability reasons. Force Majeure shall not include, 
with respect to Customer: (a) economic hardship, changes in market conditions, or the cost 
or unavailability of financing; (b) delays in Customer’s procurement of equipment or 
failure of Customer’s suppliers or contractors, unless caused by an independent Force 
Majeure event; (c) labor disputes involving only Customer’s or its contractors’ workforce; 
(d) Customer’s failure to obtain required permits or approvals, unless it has diligently and 
timely pursued them; or (e) changes in the demand for, or the business case of, the Large 
Load Facility’s end use. Interruptions resulting from the Single Contingency Design shall 
not be treated as Force Majeure. Force Majeure shall not excuse the failure to make 
payments when due or to timely post or maintain the Security. 
1.12 
“Customer’s Obligations” means Customer’s obligations commencing with the facility 
study estimated costs assigned to the Large Load subject to adjustment through the 
Interconnection Cost Allocation Process until the execution of the CRA, at which point the 
security amount and adjustments thereto shall be based on the Customer’s remaining 
payment obligations under the CRA.  
1.13 
“Draw Event” has the meaning given in Section 2.4.

1.14 
“Interconnection Cost Allocation Process” means the process by which the final 
estimated costs are allocated to Customer, as may be incorporated into NYISO’s or 
Transmission Owner’s procedures.  
1.15 
“Large Load Facility” has the meaning given in the CRA and is the “Load Facility” under 
the Large Load Interconnection Agreement. 
1.16 
“Letter of Credit” means an irrevocable standby letter of credit substantially in the form 
of Attachment A, issued by a U.S. commercial bank, a U.S. branch of a foreign commercial 
bank, or the U.S. subsidiary of a foreign commercial bank, in each case with counters in 
New York, that (i) is subject to the jurisdiction of the New York federal or state courts, (ii) 
if a foreign bank, is compliant with 12 C.F.R. Part 252 (Regulation YY), (iii) has assets of 
at least [$1,000,000,000], and (iv) has a Credit Rating of at least [“A-” from S&P and “A3” 
from Moody’s] (the “Minimum Issuer Rating”); provided that if the bank is rated by only 
one of those agencies and the bank is approved in writing by an authorized representative 
of Transmission Owner, only the Minimum Issuer Rating for that agency must be satisfied. 
Each Letter of Credit shall have an expiration date at least twelve (12) months after its date 
of issuance or renewal and shall be renewed, replaced, extended and maintained until the 
Security Release Date. All Letter of Credit costs shall be borne by Customer. 
1.17 
“Moody’s” means Moody’s Investors Service, Inc. or its successor. 
1.18 
“Network Upgrades”: Additions, modifications, enhancements, or replacements to the 
Transmission Owner’s electric transmission system required at or beyond the Point of 
Interconnection to accommodate the Customer’s Large Load Facility reliably under 
NERC, NPCC, NYSRC, and Transmission Owner reliability criteria and identified through 
the Large Load Interconnection Procedures contained at Attachment LL of the NYISO 
OATT (or successor tariff provisions) and set forth in [the CRA, the Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement, and/or other applicable agreement], for which Customer is 
providing Security under this Agreement.  
1.19 
“Project Facilities” means the Network Upgrades and TO Attachment Facilities for which 
Customer is providing Security under this Agreement. 
1.20 
“Related Agreements” means, collectively, the CRA, the Large Load Interconnection 
Agreement, and any other agreements listed in Attachment B.  
1.21  “S&P” means S&P Global Ratings or its successor. 
1.22 
“Security” means (a) Cash, (b) one or more Letters of Credit, or (c) any combination of 
the foregoing, provided and maintained in accordance with this Agreement; and, with 
respect to any increase or decrease in the Security Amount, Cash, a substitute Letter of 
Credit, or an amendment to a previously delivered Letter of Credit, unless otherwise agreed 
in writing by Transmission Owner. 
1.23 
“Security Amount” means, on any date, the Initial Project Security Amount or Project 
Security Amount, as increased or reduced in accordance with Sections 2.6 and 2.7. 
1.24 
“Security Posting Date” means each date set forth in Schedule 1 and each other date on 
which Customer is required to post, replace or increase Security, or on which a reduction 
in the Security Amount becomes effective under this Agreement.

1.25 
“Security Release Date” has the meaning given in Section 2.5. 
1.26 
“TO Attachment Facilities”: All facilities and equipment owned or controlled by 
Transmission Owner between the Point of Interconnection and the Point of Change of 
Ownership that are constructed or modified for the purpose of interconnecting the Large 
Load Facility, including line taps, breakers, disconnect switches, bus work, metering 
instrument transformers (if owned by Transmission Owner), System Protection Facilities 
at a Transmission Owner substation, and associated civil and structural works, as described 
in [the Large Load Interconnection Agreement or other applicable agreement], for which 
Customer is providing Security under this Agreement. 
ARTICLE II: SECURITY 
2.1 
Posting and Maintenance of Security. On or before each Security Posting Date, 
Customer shall provide Transmission Owner Security for Customer’s Obligations in the 
then-applicable Security Amount, and Customer shall maintain Security in the Security 
Amount at all times until the Security Release Date. Cash shall be wired to Transmission 
Owner in accordance with Transmission Owner’s written instructions delivered at least 
five (5) Business Days before the applicable Security Posting Date; if Transmission Owner 
delivers its instructions later, Customer’s deadline shall be extended until two (2) Business 
Days after receipt of the instructions. Each Letter of Credit shall be in form and substance 
acceptable to Transmission Owner. Customer shall provide a draft of each Letter of Credit 
to Transmission Owner for review at least five (5) Business Days before the applicable 
Security Posting Date. Transmission Owner shall have the opportunity to verify that the 
issuing bank satisfies the requirements of this Agreement, and the original Letter of Credit 
shall be delivered to Transmission Owner by hand delivery or overnight mail. 
(a)  
The Initial Project Security Amount shall be established by reference to the initial 
cost estimate for Network Upgrades and/or TO Attachment Facilities identified by 
System Impact Studies and Facilities Studies under Attachment LL of the NYISO 
OATT or successor tariff provisions. This amount shall be entered at Schedule 1.  
(b)  
The Security Amount shall be adjusted as prescribed in Sections 2.5, 2.6 and 2.7 of 
this Agreement and Article 6 of the CRA.  
2.2 
Letter of Credit Renewals and Replacements; Downgrades.  
(a) 
Renewal. If a Letter of Credit is scheduled to expire before the Security Release 
Date, Customer shall renew or replace it no later than ninety (90) days before its 
expiration. If the issuing bank gives a non-extension notice, Customer shall provide 
acceptable replacement Security within five (5) Business Days after receiving that 
notice and in all events before the Letter of Credit expires. The renewed or 
replacement Letter of Credit shall expire no earlier than the later of (i) one (1) year 
after its issuance or renewal and (ii) the Security Release Date. Customer shall send 
evidence of the renewed or replaced Letter of Credit from the issuing bank to 
Transmission Owner within five (5) Business Days after renewal or replacement. 
(b) 
Issuer Downgrade. If an issuing bank fails to maintain the Minimum Issuer Rating 
(an “Issuer Downgrade”), Customer shall deliver a substitute Letter of Credit within

five (5) Business Days after the Customer knew or should have known of the Issuer 
Downgrade. 
(c) 
Return of Replaced Letter of Credit. Upon receipt and acceptance of a substitute 
or replacement Letter of Credit, Transmission Owner shall, within five (5) Business 
Days after Customer’s request, return the replaced Letter of Credit to the issuing 
bank and notify Customer, unless Transmission Owner has drawn on it or a Draw 
Event is continuing. 
• 2.3 
Substitution of Security. If Customer replaces Cash with a Letter of Credit, or 
replaces a Letter of Credit with Cash or a Letter of Credit, in each case in an amount at 
least equal to the then-applicable Security Amount, Transmission Owner shall, within 
thirty (30) calendar days after receipt of the replacement Security, refund the replaced Cash 
or return the replaced Letter of Credit, as applicable, unless a Draw Event has occurred and 
is continuing. During any period in which Transmission Owner holds Security exceeding 
the Security Amount, Transmission Owner shall not apply, set off or draw on Security in 
an amount greater than the Security Amount. Cash refunds shall be made by wire in 
accordance with Customer’s written instructions delivered at least two (2) Business Days 
before the wire. 
2.4 
Draw Events. Transmission Owner may apply, set off and/or draw on the Security, up to 
the outstanding Security Amount, upon the occurrence of any of the following (each, a 
“Draw Event”): 
(a) 
Customer notifies Transmission Owner in writing that it is ceasing to negotiate, or 
fails, within a reasonable period of time, to enter into the CRA, the Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement, or other applicable agreements, and either NYISO or 
the Transmission Owner has informed Customer in writing that the Project 
Facilities must be completed because they are included in the NYISO base case, 
Transmission Owner’s local transmission plan, or the NYISO’s Reliability Needs 
Assessment or Short-Term Assessment of Reliability or another interconnection 
request relies on completion of the Network Upgrades or TO Attachment Facilities; 
[(b)  
Customer notifies Transmission Owner in writing that it is ceasing to negotiate, or 
fails, within a reasonable period of time, to enter into the CRA, the Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement, or other applicable agreements, and NYISO or 
Transmission Owner has determined that the Project Facilities are not needed, to 
the extent of costs to restore the New York State Transmission System to a safe and 
reliable condition;] 
(c) 
An Event of Default has occurred under any Related Agreement and any applicable 
Cure Period has expired; 
(d) 
Customer Abandons the Large Load Facility or a material portion of it, and the 
abandonment continues for thirty (30) days after Transmission Owner’s written 
notice to Customer; 
(e)  
Customer fails to pay any amount, or any amount finally determined to be due, 
when due, under the CRA, and the failure continues beyond any applicable Cure 
Period;

(f)  
The CRA has terminated prior to the expiration of the Assessment Period 
thereunder; 
(g) 
A Letter of Credit will expire in thirty (30) days or less, or an earlier period required 
by Section 2.2(a), and Customer has not renewed or replaced it as required by 
Section 2.2(a); 
(h) 
Customer fails to deliver substitute or replacement Security within the time required 
by Section 2.2(b); 
(i) 
Customer fails to comply with a material term of this Agreement, or defaults under 
a material term of any Related Agreements, and the failure continues beyond any 
applicable Cure Period after Transmission Owner’s written notice describing the 
default; or 
(j) 
Transmission Owner is otherwise entitled to draw on Security under any Related 
Agreement. 
Upon a Draw Event, Transmission Owner may draw on or make demand under any or all of the 
Security without further notice to Customer. If Transmission Owner draws before it incurs the 
related costs, it shall hold the proceeds as Cash Security and apply them only to Customer’s 
Obligations in accordance with Section 2.5. Customer shall remain liable for all Customer’s 
Obligations that remain unpaid after application of the Security. 
2.5  
Application and Release of Security. Transmission Owner may apply any or all of the 
Security to Customer’s Obligations, including amounts owed by Customer to complete the 
Project Facilities or restore the New York State Transmission System to a safe and reliable 
condition. Upon a Draw Event, Transmission Owner shall apply the drawn funds (the 
“Funds”) to then-outstanding Customer’s Obligations and shall retain any Funds exceeding 
those obligations (“Excess Proceeds”) as security for future Customer’s Obligations. 
Within thirty (30) calendar days after the latest of the following dates (the “Security 
Release Date”), Transmission Owner shall refund any unapplied Cash and Excess Proceeds 
to Customer, and/or return any unapplied Letter of Credit to the issuing bank: 
(i)  
the date on which all of Customer’s obligations under the Related Agreements have 
been satisfied; 
(ii)  
the date on which the portions of the New York State Transmission System affected 
by construction of the Project Facilities have been restored to a safe and reliable 
condition, as confirmed in writing by NYISO or Transmission Owner, and all 
associated costs have been paid, as applicable, and all of Customer’s obligations 
under the Related Agreements have been satisfied (the “Restoration Completion 
Date”); or  
(iii)  
the date on which Transmission Owner or NYISO confirms in writing that the 
Project Facilities are no longer required, Customer has paid all outstanding 
obligations, neither Party has any current or future obligation to restore the New 
York State Transmission System or to install or complete any Project Facilities, and 
all of Customer’s obligations under the Related Agreements have been satisfied 
(the “Obligation Termination Date”).

Cash refunds shall be wired to Customer in accordance with Customer’s written instructions 
delivered at least two (2) Business Days before the wire. Any interest earned on Cash Security or 
Excess Proceeds shall be for the account of Transmission Owner. Notwithstanding Section 9-207 
of the New York Uniform Commercial Code and to the extent permitted by applicable law, 
Transmission Owner may invest, use, commingle or otherwise dispose of Cash Security and 
Excess Proceeds, subject to its obligations to apply or return those amounts under this Agreement. 
2.6 
 Reduction or Increase of Security Amount as a Result of the Interconnection Cost 
Allocation Process and/or the CRA. 
Customer must timely post Security in the Initial Project Security Amount, subject to 
adjustment based on the Interconnection Cost Allocation Process in effect at the time of 
the Facilities Study. The Interconnection Cost Allocation Process shall provide the 
procedures pursuant to which cost allocations are adjusted when projects fail timely to post 
security following the release of the Facilities Studies until all remaining projects in the 
Cluster have posted required security. Required Security may also be adjusted upon 
execution of the CRA and adjusted annually thereafter to provide security for Customer’s 
obligations under the CRA for the remaining term. 
If Customer provided a Letter of Credit as Security, the annual adjustment may occur at 
the time of renewal of the Letter of Credit by amendment or replacement of the Letter of 
Credit. If Customer provided Cash as Security, the annual adjustment shall be effectuated 
through either an increase in the Cash provided by Customer or a refund of Cash held by 
Transmission Owner. Within ten (10) Business Days after Customer’s written request 
following a reduction of the Security Amount, Transmission Owner shall refund by wire 
any Cash exceeding the adjusted Security Amount or return any replaced Letter of Credit 
(provided Customer has delivered a substitute Letter of Credit or amendment in the 
adjusted Security Amount) to the issuing bank. Changes to Schedule 1 under this Section 
shall not constitute an amendment of this Agreement. 
2.7 
Adjustment of Security Amount as a result of Change in Scope or Extension Request. 
The Security Amount shall be adjusted for reasons including but not limited to the 
following occurrences, and in each case as may be reflected in an amendment to the Large 
Load Interconnection Agreement and/or CRA: 
(i)  
Change in Scope. If the scope of the Project Facilities is modified, expanded or 
otherwise changed from the scope described in the Large Load Interconnection 
Agreement, CRA, or other applicable agreements, including as a result of a Material 
Modification or an Exceedance Event under the Large Load Interconnection 
Agreement or updated engineering or design requirements, the Security Amount 
shall be adjusted by the amount of the change in Customer’s allocated share of the 
costs of the Project Facilities attributable to that change. Transmission Owner shall 
provide Customer with a written calculation of the adjustment. 
(ii)  
Extension Request; Suspension or Delay. If Customer requests an extension of 
any milestone date in the Large Load Interconnection Agreement, CRA, or other 
applicable agreements, or suspends or delays performance under Section 3.3 of the 
CRA, and the extension, suspension or delay results in additional costs to 
Transmission Owner under the Large Load Interconnection Agreement or CRA,

the Security Amount shall be increased by the amount of those additional costs, as 
reasonably documented by Transmission Owner. Transmission Owner shall not 
require the increased Security Amount earlier than five (5) Business Days after 
delivering that documentation to Customer. 
On the applicable Security Posting Date for an adjustment, Customer shall post additional Security 
in a form permitted by Section 2.1 if the Security Amount increases, or Transmission Owner shall 
take the actions described in Section 2.6 if the Security Amount decreases. Any increased Security 
Amount remains subject to reduction under Section 2.6. 
ARTICLE III: TERM 
3.1 
Term. This Agreement is effective as of the Effective Date and continues until the later of 
(i) the Security Release Date and (ii) the date on which Transmission Owner has returned 
or released all unapplied Security to Customer in accordance with Section 2.5. Rights and 
obligations that by their nature survive expiration or termination shall so survive.  
ARTICLE IV: NOTICES 
4.1 
Notices. Notices shall be in writing and delivered by hand, United States mail, overnight 
courier, or email (provided that an email notice is also delivered by one of the other 
methods). Notices are effective on receipt. A Party may change its address by notice given 
in accordance with this Section. 
If to Transmission Owner: [Name], [Address], Attn: [Treasurer / Vice President], 
Phone: [___], Email: [___]; with a copy to: [Address], Attn: General Counsel. 
If to Customer: [Name], [Address], Attn: [___], Phone: [___], Email: [___]. 
ARTICLE V: MISCELLANEOUS 
5.1 
Representations and Warranties. As of the Effective Date, each Party represents and 
warrants to the other that: (i) it is duly organized, validly existing and in good standing 
under the laws of its jurisdiction of formation; (ii) it has all regulatory authorizations 
necessary to perform its obligations under this Agreement; (iii) its execution, delivery and 
performance of this Agreement are within its powers, have been duly authorized, and do 
not violate its governing documents or, in any material respect, any contract to which it is 
a party or any applicable law; and (iv) this Agreement is its legal, valid and binding 
obligation, enforceable in accordance with its terms, subject to bankruptcy, insolvency and 
similar laws and to general principles of equity. 
5.2  
Assignment. This Agreement may be assigned by a Party only with the other Party’s 
written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed; provided that 
(a) Transmission Owner may assign without consent to an Affiliate or successor with the 
legal authority and operational ability to perform; (b) Transmission Owner may assign 
without consent in connection with a sale, merger, restructuring, or transfer of all or 
substantially all of its assets, including the Project Facilities, if the assignee assumes in 
writing all obligations hereunder; and (c) Customer may assign without consent for 
collateral security purposes to aid in financing the Large Load Facility, upon prompt notice 
to Transmission Owner. Any assignment by Customer (other than a collateral assignment) 
and any change of control of Customer shall require Transmission Owner’s prior written

consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, and shall be conditioned 
on (i) the assignee assuming in writing all obligations under this Agreement and the Related 
Agreements; (ii) the assignee posting replacement Security under this Agreement before 
the assignment becomes effective and having a Credit Rating equal to or greater than that 
of Customer as of the date of assignment or providing such additional Security under this 
Agreement as Transmission Owner reasonably requires; and (iii) Customer reimbursing 
Transmission Owner’s reasonable costs of administering the assignment or performing due 
diligence with respect to a change in control, including reissuing invoices and amending 
related contracts. Any financing obtained by Customer shall require the secured party to 
notify Transmission Owner before exercising assignment rights and to demonstrate 
compliance with Section 6.2 and Article 18 of the Large Load Interconnection Agreement. 
Any assignment in violation of this Section is void. No assignment by Customer shall 
release Customer or any existing Security until the assignee’s replacement Security has 
been posted and accepted. No assignment shall relieve a Party of, or enlarge, its obligations. 
5.3 
Governing Law. THIS AGREEMENT AND THE RIGHTS AND DUTIES OF THE 
PARTIES HEREUNDER SHALL BE GOVERNED BY AND CONSTRUED, 
ENFORCED AND PERFORMED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE LAWS OF THE 
STATE OF NEW YORK, WITHOUT REGARD TO PRINCIPLES OF CONFLICTS OF 
LAW. 
5.4 
FERC, the OATT, and Related Agreements Compliance. The Parties shall comply with 
all applicable filing, acceptance, and effectiveness requirements under Federal Power Act 
Section 205, the OATT, and Related Agreements. No amendment or waiver that is required 
to be filed with and accepted by FERC shall be effective before the required filing or 
acceptance, and the Parties shall cooperate in making any required filing. 
5.5 
Counterparts and Electronic Signatures. This Agreement may be executed in 
counterparts, each of which is an original and all of which together are one instrument. 
Counterparts and signatures delivered by email in PDF format or through an electronic-
signature platform are effective as originals. 
5.6 
Binding Effect. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the 
Parties and their successors and permitted assigns.  
5.7 
Rules of Interpretation. Unless a contrary intention clearly appears: the singular includes 
the plural; references to any agreement, tariff, or law mean it as amended from time to 
time; references to Articles, Sections, Schedules, and Attachments are to this Agreement 
unless otherwise indicated with respect to a Related Agreement; “including” means 
including without limitation; “hereunder,” “herein” and similar words refer to this 
Agreement as a whole; and “from” means “from and including,” “to” means “to but 
excluding,” and “through” means “through and including.”   
5.8 
Several Obligations. The obligations of the Parties are several, and not joint, and not joint 
and several. 
5.9 
Entire Agreement; Related Agreements. This Agreement and the Related Agreements 
are intended to operate together and shall be interpreted consistently with one another. This 
Agreement, including its Schedule, Attachments, and the Related Agreements, constitutes

the entire agreement of the Parties with respect to its subject matter and supersedes all prior 
understandings, oral or written. 
5.10  No Third-Party Beneficiaries; No Partnership. This Agreement does not create rights, 
remedies, or benefits in favor of any person other than the Parties and their successors in 
interest and, where permitted, their assigns. This Agreement shall not be construed to create 
an association, joint venture, agency relationship, or partnership among the Parties, and no 
Party shall have authority to bind any other Party.  
5.11 
Waiver. The failure of a Party to insist on strict performance on any occasion shall not be 
a waiver, and no waiver of any breach shall be a continuing waiver or a waiver of any other 
or subsequent breach.  
5.12  Force Majeure. No Party shall be considered in default of any obligation under this 
Agreement to the extent its performance is prevented or delayed by any event of Force 
Majeure, provided that such Party gives prompt written notice and uses reasonable efforts 
to resume performance; provided that Force Majeure shall not excuse any obligation to pay 
money or to post, maintain, renew, replace, or increase Security. 
5.13  Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is finally determined to be invalid or 
unenforceable by a court or Governmental Authority, the remaining provisions shall 
continue in full force and effect. 
5.14  Order of Precedence. In the event of a conflict between this Agreement and any Related 
Agreement regarding Security, this Agreement controls; in the event of a conflict regarding

Parties, subject to any required filing with and acceptance by FERC.
